children: Indonesia will open 200 million new bank accounts with two state lenders for citizens entering adulthood and others who do not yet have one, its senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto said on Tuesday, as Jakarta seeks to improve financial inclusion.
Each account will receive at least 50,000 rupiah ($2.84) from the government, Airlangga told reporters.
The minister also said proposals were being discussed to allow citizens to receive a bank account automatically when they turn 17 and are issued an identity card.
The two lenders are PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia
Airlangga also said that the accounts could be used to distribute government social assistance.
